name: regenerate_plugin_boilerplate
description: Picks up a template/tooling fix (a change to how this tool set generates plugin.py/main.py/version.py/install.sh) on a plugin that was already generated, without re-supplying the whole original generate_plugin_scaffold call. Reads back generation_inputs.json (written by generate_plugin_scaffold itself) and re-renders plugin.py, main.py, version.py, and install.sh with today's template code -- the existing override_bodies/authorize/ai_enabled/etc. are reused exactly as originally supplied, nothing LLM-authored needs to be retyped. Never touches server_entry.json (its live, host-assigned nsid would be lost), profile.json, README.md, LICENSE.md, tests, or node-class files -- those are content, not template output. Also the right tool for a pure version bump with nothing else changing: pass 'version' and it updates version.py, generation_inputs.json's own version field, and appends a context.md entry -- no evidence or discovery-tool call needed first, since a version bump alone introduces no new content to source. Fails clearly if generation_inputs.json doesn't exist yet (plugins generated before this tool existed need one generate_plugin_scaffold call first). A file is only actually overwritten on disk when its re-rendered content genuinely differs from what's already there -- e.g. a pure version bump with no template changes in play leaves plugin.py/main.py/install.sh untouched, since none of their content depends on the version number. The result's 'regenerated' list names exactly the files that were actually written; 'unchanged' names the ones that were checked and left alone. Tell the developer before calling this that it may touch plugin.py/main.py/install.sh if templates changed since this plugin was last generated or refreshed -- then report back which files the result says were actually regenerated vs. unchanged, don't assume all four changed. Refreshes OS permissions and notifies the platform only for the files actually written, once after writing -- a hub-side failure there is reported back as a non-fatal 'permissions_refresh_error'/'files_changed_notify_error' field and never means the change itself failed; both are omitted entirely when nothing was written.

location.description: The subdirectory name under the server's plugin output root -- the same 'location' generate_plugin_scaffold/read_generated_plugin use.

version.description: Optional. When given and different from this plugin's currently stored version, performs a pure version bump: renders version.py with this value, updates generation_inputs.json's version field, and appends a context.md entry. Omit to just refresh the 4 template files with today's code, unchanged version.

iteration_note.description: Optional free-text note for the context.md entry when version is given and actually changes -- defaults to a plain 'Version bumped X -> Y.' note if omitted. Ignored when version is omitted or unchanged.
